title: Same heatwave, different barriers
label: who heat hits hardest
text: Two neighbours in a farming village face the same heatwave: a woman farming rainfed land and an older man who uses a wheelchair. Four questions show where their routes to safety split, and what each needs to reach the same outcome: livelihood security and dignity. The people are illustrative composites.

title: Where the gaps may be
label: the heat network
text: When this film was made, 136 organisations on our list worked on heat, crowding onto worker protection and health, and five loops had nobody listed. A low count shows a gap in this directory’s coverage, not proof that nobody is working on it.

title: How this map works
label: about this map
text: An illustrative systems map: switching an action on shows which cycles it could help interrupt, not what it will achieve. Three kinds of evidence, what the badges mean, and where to find ratings of what works and what it costs.

title: Four heats in a home
label: cooling options
text: Outdoor air, the roof, radiant heat from the ceiling and the air inside: why a tin-roofed home can stay hot long after the street cools, why informal settlements are hit harder, and what reflective roofs can do.

title: Weather, work and the person
label: who heat hits hardest
text: Two people stand in the same heat. Heat strain is where the weather, the work and the person meet: humidity and hot nights, heavy effort and protective clothing, age, illness and some medicines. Who heat plans miss, and three questions to ask for every group. Not medical advice.
